purpose: OFFICIAL-scope full Online-Mind2Web run: all 300 tasks, zero exclusions. Frozen BEFORE any task is run.

task_file.order: upstream raw.json order (runs/mind2web_import/raw.json, fetched 2026-07-10 from hud-evals/Online-Mind2Web datasets-server mirror, CC-BY-4.0)
task_file.level_rule: official level when present, else reference_length <=5 easy / 6-10 medium / >=11 hard (arXiv:2504.01382 §2.2) — identical to both committed 20-task subsets
task_file.conversion: same normalize()/to_subset_entry() code path as tools/import_mind2web.py (BrowserTaskContract schema-gated per entry); official fields task_id/confirmed_task/website preserved as source_task_id/natural_language_task/website, level as difficulty

no_exclusion_declaration.statement: NO exclusions of any kind: the subset importer's excluded_domains list and login-task-text regex are deliberately NOT applied. Login/shopping/anti-bot-walled tasks are all included.
no_exclusion_declaration.handling: When the capability guard refuses a login/purchase task or a site blocks automation, that refusal/block is recorded and reported honestly as part of the official-scope result (env-error taxonomy still classifies rows post-hoc; nothing is removed from the task set up front).

overlap_with_prior_subsets.statement: All 40 previously-run tasks (20 dev subset + 20 held-out) are a strict subset of these 300. This full run is a separate OFFICIAL-scope measurement; it does not modify, rerun, or invalidate the two prior subset runs, whose conclusions stand as reported. The held-out set's no-rerun freeze applies to that set's own protocol, not to this independent official-scope pass.

runner_semantics_verified.limit: --limit N slices the first N ACTIVE tasks in task-file order (entries = [active tasks]; entries[:N]) — applied AFTER the status=='active' filter and BEFORE any resume check. All 300 full300 tasks are active, so --limit N == first N tasks in file order.
runner_semantics_verified.resume: --resume checks, per task inside the (possibly limited) entry list, load_done_summary(task_id, out_root=--out): reuses the prior row iff <out>/summaries/<task_id> summary has harness_status=='done' AND a row (row gets resumed=True, not re-executed). Summaries with harness_status 'error' or 'incomplete' (pre-marker left by a mid-task crash) are NOT reused — those tasks re-run. scan_incomplete() reports crash leftovers separately.
runner_semantics_verified.combination: --limit slices BEFORE resume filtering, so '--limit N --resume' never advances the window past completed tasks; chunked runs must use CUMULATIVE --limit values with the SAME --out dir (see chunk_plan). Resumed rows still enter metrics/results.json, so the final chunk's results.json covers all 300.

chunks.covers: tasks 241-300 (1-240 resumed); its results.json is the full-300 rollup

chunk_plan.abort_note: should_abort (>ERROR_ABORT_RATE of attempted after ERROR_ABORT_MIN) can stop a chunk early; a re-launch of the same chunk with --resume re-runs only non-done tasks. Resumed rows do not count toward n_attempted, so the abort ratio resets per launch.
